answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a contract before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independently verified fraud is proven. One operator can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital, so a sybil swarm has a real opportunity cost and risks losing its stake. A nectar or onyx label, or a terrace of freshly minted accounts, cannot substitute for the collateral; the defense raises the price of attack rather than claiming to make identities impossible.
